title: Cedar policy slicing: instantiate the general sound-slice theorem at the scope-based bound analysis
intent: Reduce the theorem that scope-based slicing preserves `isAuthorized` to three chained instantiations of a general sound-slice framework. The glue `apply`s the general sound-slice theorem `isAuthorized_eq_for_sound_policy_slice`, then the bridge `sound_bound_analysis_produces_sound_slices` that turns a sound bound analysis into a sound slice, and closes with the leaf `scope_analysis_is_sound`.
also_known_as: prove the general soundness theorem once, instantiate at the concrete analysis

parent.name: isAuthorized_eq_for_scope_based_policy_slice
parent.statement:
theorem isAuthorized_eq_for_scope_based_policy_slice (request : Request) (entities : Entities) (policies : Policies) :
  isAuthorized request entities (BoundAnalysis.slice scopeAnalysis request entities policies) =
  isAuthorized request entities policies

children.name: isAuthorized_eq_for_sound_policy_slice
children.statement:
theorem isAuthorized_eq_for_sound_policy_slice (req : Request) (entities : Entities) (slice policies : Policies) :
  IsSoundPolicySlice req entities slice policies →
  isAuthorized req entities slice = isAuthorized req entities policies
children.note: The general statement, proved once for every sound slice: when `slice` is a sound slice of `policies` for `req`/`entities`, `isAuthorized` agrees on the two. Its proof splits the two outcomes — `satisfiedPolicies_eq_for_sound_policy_slice .forbid` / `.permit` give the satisfied-policy sets, `errorPolicies_eq_for_sound_policy_slice` the error sets — and recombines with `isAuthorized_eq_of_satisfied_and_error_policies_eq`; all three are imported from the authorization theory, not proved here.

children.name: sound_bound_analysis_produces_sound_slices
children.statement:
theorem sound_bound_analysis_produces_sound_slices (ba : BoundAnalysis) (request : Request) (entities : Entities) (policies : Policies) :
  IsSoundBoundAnalysis ba →
  IsSoundPolicySlice request entities (ba.slice request entities policies) policies
children.closed_by: unfold of IsSoundBoundAnalysis, IsSoundPolicySlice, BoundAnalysis.slice, IsSoundPolicyBound, then simp_all (left) and by_contra + simp (right)
children.note: The bridge: a sound bound analysis `ba` yields a sound slice. Its proof is pure unfolding — `IsSoundBoundAnalysis`, `IsSoundPolicySlice`, `BoundAnalysis.slice`, then `IsSoundPolicyBound` — and the two conjuncts close by `simp_all` (subset direction) and by contradiction (`by_contra` + `simp`). It cites no named lemma, so it is a leaf of the lemma graph but not a one-liner.

children.name: scope_analysis_is_sound
children.note: The leaf: `scopeAnalysis` is a sound bound analysis, closed in one line by `simp [IsSoundBoundAnalysis, scope_bound_is_sound]`, delegating the per-policy work to `scope_bound_is_sound` (in this file), which itself closes on the four scope lemmas imported from the authorization theory.

applicability.goal_shape: A theorem about a concrete analysis or slicing (`BoundAnalysis.slice scopeAnalysis`) that is a special case of a general soundness statement (`isAuthorized_eq_for_sound_policy_slice`) over an abstract predicate (`IsSoundPolicySlice`), reached through a bridge (`sound_bound_analysis_produces_sound_slices`) that reduces the concrete soundness obligation to one abstract predicate (`IsSoundBoundAnalysis`) and a leaf proving that predicate for the concrete analysis.
applicability.use_when: the general statement is already proved over an abstract soundness/slicing predicate, and the concrete case needs only (a) a bridge lemma mapping the concrete construction onto that predicate and (b) a leaf proving the concrete analysis meets the predicate's own hypotheses, so the parent proof is pure `apply`/`exact` with no new mathematics.
applicability.avoid_when: the concrete construction does not literally satisfy the abstract predicate's shape (then the bridge must do real work rather than unfold); the leaf that the concrete analysis is sound is itself a substantial theorem rather than a one-line `simp`; or the general statement is not already proved, in which case proving it is the real content and the instantiation is trivial by comparison.

consequences: Creates three obligations, one per child, and the glue is a pure chain of `apply`/`exact` with no new goal manipulation. (1) The general sound-slice theorem `isAuthorized_eq_for_sound_policy_slice`, the expensive part, which itself imports three per-outcome lemmas. (2) The bridge `sound_bound_analysis_produces_sound_slices`, which reduces `IsSoundPolicySlice` for `ba.slice ...` to `IsSoundBoundAnalysis ba` and is discharged entirely by unfolding definitions. (3) The leaf `scope_analysis_is_sound`, a one-line `simp` over `scope_bound_is_sound`. Failure modes: if the concrete slice is not literally `BoundAnalysis.slice analysis ...` for some `analysis` satisfying `IsSoundBoundAnalysis`, the bridge does not apply and the general sound-slice argument must be redone; if the leaf's soundness is not `simp`-trivial (its per-policy soundness rests on the scope lemmas elsewhere, which are the real content), the instantiation is not free.
